title: Sell Mineral Rights in Mars, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Mars, PA | Butler County
metaDescription: Own minerals under farmland near Mars, PA? We buy Butler County Marcellus interests directly, explain your division order, and close on your timeline.
heroLead: Butler County land north of Pittsburgh has been quietly leased and drilled for a generation, and a lot of the families holding those minerals never planned to be in the gas business.
intro: Mars sits in the northern reach of Butler County, close enough to the Allegheny River corridor that operators have run Marcellus wet-gas pads through the surrounding townships for years without most residents thinking much about it. If your family's name is on a lease from Adams or Cranberry Township, or you inherited a fractional interest from a grandparent's farm that got broken up when the borough grew up around it, you already know how confusing the paperwork gets.

We buy mineral and royalty interests in this part of Butler County directly, no listing, no waiting on a broker to find a buyer. We look at your deed history, your current division order, and whatever royalty statements you have, then make an offer that reflects what the interest is actually doing today, not what someone promised it might do.

sections.heading: Butler County's Wet-Gas Window
paragraphs: Butler sits inside the wetter part of the Marcellus fairway, which means production here carries a mix of natural gas, ethane, and propane rather than pure dry gas. That mix matters for pricing because liquids-rich gas gets processed before it's sold, and processing costs are exactly where post-production deductions eat into a royalty check.

Operators active around Mars and neighboring Butler County townships have run multi-well pads with laterals reaching well past a mile, which is why so many small legacy tracts near the borough ended up pooled into units their original owners never signed a lease for directly. If you're holding an interest by inheritance rather than by your own lease, that's a common story here, not an unusual one.

sections.heading: What We Look At Before Making an Offer
paragraphs: We start with the Butler County Recorder of Deeds records to confirm the chain of title, then pull your current division order to see what decimal interest you're actually being paid on. A lot of Mars-area interests trace back to farms split among siblings decades ago, so the fractional math can be more complicated than the deed itself suggests.

From there we look at 12 to 24 months of royalty history if you have it. That trailing production tells us far more than a well's original completion numbers, since Marcellus wells decline fast in the first few years and level off afterward.

sections.heading: Deductions and the Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act
paragraphs: Pennsylvania's Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act sets a floor at one-eighth of production, but plenty of leases signed before that protection or drafted around it still leave gathering, compression, and dehydration costs coming straight off your check before you see a dollar. If your statement shows deductions eating a large share of gross value, you're not imagining it, and you're not alone in Butler County.
We don't need you to untangle that math yourself. Send us what you have and we'll walk through it with you plainly before any number gets discussed.

faqs.question: Do you buy interests near Mars that are still leased but not yet producing?
faqs.answer: Yes. We evaluate leased but non-producing interests based on the operator, the lease terms, and how active drilling has been in that specific township, and we'll tell you honestly if we think waiting makes more sense for you.

faqs.question: I only have a fractional interest inherited from my grandfather's farm. Is that worth anything?
faqs.answer: Small fractional interests are common around Mars because so much of the original farmland here was subdivided over generations. Even a modest decimal interest tied to an active unit can have real value, so it's worth sending us the details.

faqs.question: How fast can this close?
faqs.answer: Once we've confirmed title through the Butler County Recorder of Deeds, most straightforward transfers close within a few weeks. Complicated estates with unresolved probate take longer, and we'll tell you that up front.
